answer: A stake-bonded work record resists sybils in an agent economy: before an agent can earn, it locks a bond released only after its attestations verify on-chain. Forging identities is cheap, but each one must burn real compute and keep an ember of verifiable history alive, or its bond is slashed. A farmer spawning sock-puppets pays linear cost per identity, while honest agents branch like cedar from one trunk: their root stake is one-time, so the attacker's cost never drops. Duplicate proofs leave an umber trail, and mass forgery bankrupts the forger first.
